body.title: Send invoice throws TypeError and does nothing on the invoice create page (#send-invoice)
body.summary: The user created an invoice, saved it as a draft successfully, then clicked Send invoice. The click threw an uncaught TypeError in sendInvoice, the user rage-clicked the button five times, and nothing was sent.

steps_to_reproduce.text: Open the invoices list page.
Click New invoice.
On the new invoice page, enter a customer.
Enter 1250.00 as the amount.
Click Save draft.
Click Send invoice.
Click Send invoice repeatedly (5 rapid clicks).
Click Back.

body.expected: Clicking Send invoice sends the saved invoice and shows a confirmation or status change.
body.actual: Clicking Send invoice throws an uncaught TypeError (Cannot read properties of undefined reading 'id') in sendInvoice at InvoiceSendButton.tsx:48:21. The invoice is not sent, and the user rage-clicks the button.

evidence.note: Save draft POST to /api/invoices returned 201, so the draft was created before the send attempt.
Uncaught TypeError in sendInvoice (InvoiceSendButton.tsx:48:21) fires on the Send invoice click.
Console error logs the same TypeError, confirming it is unhandled.
Five rapid clicks on #send-invoice show the user got no feedback and kept retrying.

body.suspected_cause: A likely cause is that sendInvoice reads an .id property from a value that is undefined at InvoiceSendButton.tsx:48, possibly the saved draft or customer object not being set in the component state after Save draft.

body.title: Send reminder fails with 500 (reported by [email])
body.summary: On invoice inv_8812 the user clicked Send reminder twice, and both attempts hit the reminders endpoint. Both requests returned 500 internal_error and the UI showed a generic 'Something went wrong' message each time.

steps_to_reproduce.text: Open invoice inv_8812 at app.ledgerly.example/invoices/inv_8812.
Click the 'Send reminder' button (#send-reminder).
The POST to /api/invoices/inv_8812/reminders returns status 500 with error internal_error (request_id req_7Hk2).
The UI shows 'Something went wrong. Please try again.'
Click 'Send reminder' (#send-reminder) again.
The second POST to the same reminders endpoint returns status 500 with error internal_error (request_id req_7Hm9).
The UI shows 'Something went wrong. Please try again.' again.

body.expected: The reminder is sent for invoice inv_8812, or the user gets a specific, actionable error message.
body.actual: Both reminder requests fail with a 500 internal_error, and the user sees only a generic error message. No reminder is confirmed as sent.

evidence.note: First POST to the reminders endpoint returns 500 internal_error after 412 ms.
Generic 'Something went wrong' message appears right after the first failure.
Retry POST to the same endpoint also returns 500 internal_error, so the failure is repeatable.
Generic error message appears again, and the recording has no console errors to explain it.

body.suspected_cause: A server-side exception in the invoice reminders endpoint is likely causing the 500 responses, since the failure is consistent across retries and the body only says internal_error.

body.title: AR aging report times out with 504 for 90-day range on /reports
body.summary: The user opened the reports page and clicked AR aging, which requested the 90-day aging report. The request hit a gateway timeout after about 30 seconds, and the user rage-clicked the report while the page showed a message suggesting a shorter range.

steps_to_reproduce.text: Open the reports page at app.ledgerly.example/reports.
Click the AR aging element (#aging-report).
Wait while GET /api/reports/aging?range=90d runs until it returns status 504 after about 30 seconds.
Click the #aging-report element four times in quick succession.
Read the message 'This report is taking too long. Try a shorter range.'

body.expected: The AR aging report for the 90-day range loads within the gateway time limit and displays the data.
body.actual: The aging request returns 504 gateway_timeout after 30012 ms, the user rage-clicks the report, and the page shows a message asking them to try a shorter range.

evidence.note: The aging API call returned 504 gateway_timeout after 30012 ms, which is the failure itself.
Four rapid clicks on the report show the user was stuck waiting with no feedback.
The UI tells the user to pick a shorter range, so the failure is surfaced as a user-facing error.

body.suspected_cause: The 90-day aging query likely takes longer than the gateway timeout (about 30 seconds) on this account's data, so the backend response never arrives in time.

body.title: Payments page fails with ChunkLoadError (404 on chunk 812) after 2026.10.27-1 deploy
body.summary: The user clicked Payments from the dashboard and the browser requested the lazy-loaded chunk 812.3f9a1c.chunk.js, which returned 404. The app threw a ChunkLoadError and displayed 'Page failed to load.', and the user clicked Reload.

steps_to_reproduce.text: On the dashboard, click the Payments link in the navigation.
The app navigates to /payments.
The browser requests /static/js/812.3f9a1c.chunk.js and receives a 404.

body.expected: The Payments page loads and renders.
body.actual: The chunk request returns 404, a ChunkLoadError is thrown from lazyPayments, and the user sees 'Page failed to load.' with no way to recover except reloading.

evidence.note: Network GET for chunk 812 returns 404, the root cause of the failed load.
ChunkLoadError is thrown from requireEnsure via lazyPayments, confirming the lazy route failed.
User-facing 'Page failed to load.' message appears right after the error.
User clicks Reload, a sign they could not recover in-app.

body.suspected_cause: A likely stale or missing build artifact: the client references chunk 812.3f9a1c, which the server no longer serves after the 2026.10.27-1 deploy, possibly due to a stale cached index or incomplete asset upload.

body.title: Customer CSV export returns 500 and session data exposes email, token, and card number
body.summary: The user searched customers by email, typed a card number into a field, and clicked Export CSV. The export request returned 500 export_failed, and the page showed 'Export failed.' while the recording captured the email, session token, and card number in plain text.

steps_to_reproduce.text: Open the customers page with the search query set to dana.reyes@harborfreight-supply.example.
The page logs a debug message that includes the email and a session token.
Type the card number 4242 4242 4242 4242 into the #card-number field.
Click Export CSV.
The export request GET /api/customers/export?format=csv&email=... returns HTTP 500 with error export_failed after about 920 ms.
The console logs an error with the email, and the UI shows 'Export failed.'

body.expected: The CSV export downloads successfully. Email, session tokens, and card numbers do not appear in URLs, console logs, or captured session recordings.
body.actual: The export endpoint returns 500 export_failed and the user sees 'Export failed.' Sensitive values (email, session token, full card number) appear in the page URL, console output, and recording.

evidence.note: Page URL carries the customer's email in the query string, which is exposed in logs and recordings.
Debug console log prints the email and a session token in plain text.
A full card number is typed into the page and captured by session replay, which is a PCI data exposure risk.
The export API returns 500 export_failed, which is the functional failure.
Console error logs the email alongside the 500 status.
The user receives the 'Export failed.' message, confirming the failed export is visible to them.

body.suspected_cause: The export endpoint likely fails server-side on requests that include an email query parameter, and the client likely logs and places PII and tokens in URLs and console output without redaction.

body.suspected_cause: A likely cause is that the refunds filter returns or yields a null row, and formatRow reads .amount without a null guard.
